main_text.p: when learned men for all this would not take warning, but would needs be meddling again, with that which the popish clergy could not endure should be touched, as Johannes de Selva, among others, in the end of his treatise De jurejurando, Erasmus in divers of his works, and Beatus Rhenanus in his argument upon Tertullian's book De pœnitentia: the fathers of Trent, within seventy-two years after that, conspired together to stop all men's mouths with an anathemaConc. Trident. sess. 14. can. 6., that should deny sacramental confession to be of divine institution, or to be necessary unto salvation. And so we are come to an end of that point.

page.notes: The footnote mark {b} follows "anathema" in the text. The footnote is printed in smaller type below the text. Faint show-through of the reverse page is visible in the lower half and was not transcribed.
